assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production large-area dungeon floor painting for a whole room, NOT a close-up of a few stones. Create a square true-overhead edge-to-edge field containing approximately TWENTY-FOUR rows of TWENTY-FOUR medieval fitted flagstones across the image, with several slab sizes. Each typical stone occupies ONLY 3 to 5 percent of the image width. Show hundreds of relatively small stones over a broad area, NOT eight large stones. Image 1 is the artistic reference; Image 2 is a material reference, but zoom out FARTHER so there are around 500 individual slabs in the image. Beautiful hand-painted dark-fantasy RPG floor, flat irregular broad flagstones with squared-off fitted edges, natural restrained bevels and thin dark mortar, mostly ash gray with quiet warm brown-gray and desaturated olive-gray variations. Fine hand-painted chipped edges and gentle age, rubbed flat centers, a weathered damp patch in the lower-right quarter with some pale worn stones and muted green in recessed mortar. No actual objects or raised rubble, quiet surface, no prominent unique symbols. Even neutral upper-left ambient illumination, no vignette, cast shadows, spotlights or orange lighting. Entire square is one continuous floor plane with no divisions, borders, text, scene furniture, wall or perspective. Opposite edges should repeat seamlessly. This is the full material field for an entire dungeon room at normal game scale.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: seamless overhead stone COPING material for premium hand-painted 2.5D dungeon wall caps. Image 1 is a style reference only. Produce a square edge-to-edge image containing EIGHT by EIGHT large broad roughly square, irregularly sized hewn blocks of medieval ash-gray limestone, laid as a continuous stone upper wall surface with narrow deep dark mortar. The stones are HEAVY SOLID CUBIC coping blocks seen perfectly from above, not floor cobbles, not wood, not wall vertical faces. Natural chipped bevels and worn mineral faces, quiet smoky cool gray with a few warm-gray stones, rich painted material but no giant cracks, no dramatic missing chunks, no green moss. Moderate contrast; upper surfaces medium gray, not pale beige, yellow or white. Soft neutral diffuse illumination; NO directional cast shadows, no vertical sides, no top-down scene perspective. Sparse hairline cracks on only a few stones, mostly beautiful rubbed natural surfaces. Good readable square-block construction at small game scale. No vignette, props, symbols, text, borders, labels, atlas grid or transparent gaps; entire image is opaque continuous material. All four outer edges must join seamlessly. Match the rich stone craftsmanship of the reference without using its atlas layout.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE production horizontal masonry wall-profile sprite on true transparent background. Image 1 is style reference only. Create a straight continuous horizontal ancient dungeon wall section, fully visible, about 3.2 times wider than tall. This is premium hand-painted dark-fantasy game architecture matching the reference. The upper FORTY PERCENT of its height is an overhead stone coping plane, broad heavy chipped coping blocks, 8 unequal large stones across the strip. The lower SIXTY PERCENT is a darker vertical stone wall face with TWO staggered courses of substantial irregular rectangular blocks, around 7 to 9 stones per course, deep narrow mortar and beautifully painted bevels, rubbed mineral faces and natural wear. Richly textured mottled limestone in warm gray and muted ash, upper coping clearly brighter than charcoal-gray vertical faces, subtle neutral upper-left illumination. Orthographic elevated view from SOUTH, horizontal wall axis perfectly horizontal, no isometric diamond or slanted wall axis, no receding perspective. Straight continuous rectangular overall construction; continuous flat baseline. Both left and right ends are CUT THROUGH the masonry for seamless continuation, NO visible side-end faces. No floor, no loose rocks, no props, no torches, no text, no atlas sheet or multiple objects. No huge cracks or green moss. Do not make a uniform stack of smooth machine-cut bricks. Clear material richness, premium RPG environment art. Keep a small transparent margin around the whole rectangular wall strip. Wide landscape composition.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE production ARCHWAY FRAME sprite with genuine transparent opening and transparent background. Image 1 is dark-fantasy stone style reference only. Draw a heavy rectangular gray-stone wall panel containing one broad low rounded arched doorway cut completely through it. Outer panel is 4 units wide and 3 units tall, straight top edge, straight bottom baseline, no visible floor. The arched transparent opening occupies the middle 65 percent of the width; its flat bottom reaches the panel bottom, its crown reaches about 15 percent below the panel top. Thick staggered stone jambs and 7 beautifully articulated radial wedge-shaped arch stones, convincing deep carved inner reveal. Weathered mottled ash-gray limestone, slightly chipped bevels, deeply recessed charcoal mortar, quiet mineral detail, restrained pale edge highlights; much richer than a simple vector arch. STRICT STRAIGHT-ON ORTHOGRAPHIC FRONT ELEVATION of the vertical surface: no top coping face, no top-down floor, no sideways end face, no tilted perspective. Neutral soft upper-left light without external cast shadow. Outer wall panel fills its rectangle except tiny natural chipped perimeter. Entire frame visible with a little transparent margin. NO DOOR LEAF, no wood, no iron gate, no torches, no background in the opening, no ground, text or labels. The hole MUST be transparent alpha, NOT painted black. Squat broad doorway rather than narrow Gothic tower. A single beautiful reusable raster architectural frame, with no existing perspective that would conflict when projected into a game wall.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production raster floor material for a premium hand-painted dark-fantasy 2D dungeon, not a mockup. Image 1 is the ART STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its beautifully painted small-scale ancient stone, not its atlas layout, labels, or objects. Create one square edge-to-edge seamless overhead floor texture. Around 18 to 22 uneven medieval flagstones across each image dimension: broad flat irregular quadrilateral slabs of several sizes, naturally fitted, not pebbles and not a uniform brick grid. Fine dark mortar and softly chipped rounded bevels, subtle mineral variation, smoky gray slate mixed with warm umber-gray and occasional desaturated olive stone. Carefully restrained age and a few hairline cracks, rubbed broad matte stone faces, small damp patches in a few joints. Elegant broad surfaces with rich painted depth and quiet detail, readability at small scale. True perpendicular overhead floor plane, neutral cool ambient light from upper-left, no orange light or cast shadows. No frame, borders, wall, emblems, furniture, text, sheet layout, large rubble or standing objects. Seamlessly repeatable across all opposite edges. This will cover approximately an entire 9x9 logical-tile room; avoid conspicuous repeated motifs. Create a large high-quality square source texture.
